topic.label: Math
topic.desc: Mathematics as working skills: algebra, calculus and differential equations, linear algebra, probability and statistics, discrete mathematics, proof and foundations, numerical methods and optimisation, and geometry and topology.

concepts: Solving and simplifying equations and inequalities, polynomials, functions, exponentials and logarithms, and abstract structures such as groups and rings.
Limits, derivatives, integrals, series and ordinary and partial differential equations, with their physical meaning.
Vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, decompositions and vector spaces.
Random variables, distributions, estimation, hypothesis tests, regression and the limits of what a sample shows.
Counting, graphs, number theory, recurrences and algorithms on finite structures.
Logic, sets, proof techniques such as induction and contradiction, and how to read and write a rigorous argument.
Computing answers approximately and checking the error: root finding, integration, linear solvers, floating point and optimisation.
Shapes, transformations, coordinates, curves and surfaces, and properties that survive stretching.
skills: Solves equations and inequalities step by step, checks each solution by substitution and lists any that were introduced by the method.
Factors polynomials, finds roots, asymptotes and symmetries and sketches the function from them.
Explains groups, rings and fields with small worked examples and checks that a given set meets the axioms.
Differentiates and integrates a function by named rules, shows each step and verifies the result by differentiating back.
Evaluates limits and decides whether a series converges, naming the test used and why it applies.
Solves ordinary and simple partial differential equations analytically or numerically and states the initial and boundary conditions used.
Solves linear systems by elimination, reports whether the solution is unique, absent or free, and checks the residual.
Computes eigenvalues, eigenvectors and decompositions such as SVD and explains what they say about the matrix.
Explains basis, span, rank and projection with small examples in two and three dimensions.
Fits candidate distributions to data, compares them with goodness of fit and states which assumptions each requires.
Chooses a test such as ANOVA, a chi-square test or a nonparametric test from the data type and design, runs it, and reports effect size and interval along with the p-value.
Fits linear and generalised regression models, checks residuals and warns when the fit is driven by a few points.
Counts arrangements and selections with permutations, combinations and inclusion and exclusion and checks small cases by listing.
Analyses paths, connectivity, colouring and flows on a graph and states the algorithm and its running time.
Works with primes, divisibility, modular arithmetic and congruences, with a worked check for each result.
Writes a proof by induction, contradiction or construction, with every step justified and the claim restated at the end.
Reads a proof line by line, marks gaps and unjustified steps and says whether the argument proves the stated claim.
Searches for small cases that break a conjecture or lemma and reports what the failure says about the claim.
Applies bisection, Newton or quadrature rules and reports the error estimate and the iteration count.
Finds rounding, cancellation and overflow problems in a computation and proposes a stabler form.
Sets up an optimisation problem with objective, variables and constraints, picks a method and checks the result is a true optimum.
Converts between coordinate systems and applies rotations, scalings and translations with matrices.
Computes length, area, curvature and tangents of curves and surfaces from a parametrisation.
Explains open sets, continuity, connectedness and homeomorphism with simple spaces and checks which properties are preserved.
